acceptanceCriteria: Record an owner-approved threat model and decision for non-loopback corpus HTTP exposure, including whether Corvint must enforce authenticated transport or retain the operator-owned boundary.

If a product-managed profile is accepted, demonstrate that unauthenticated requests cannot read corpus records and retain focused remote, interruption, and rollback evidence; otherwise provide a qualified reference deployment with TLS, access control, and direct-exposure refusal evidence.
Keep the loopback-only default and historical trust envelope unchanged; update the owning spec and record qualification limits.
body: Security audit on 2026-10-12 of origin/main d6e1eb32d09a377165d4ad5df689cd24571d3790. Reproduction: start the optional corvint-corpus-http with --allow-remote and a non-loopback --listen address, then POST a valid JSON request to /query from a reachable host. cmd/corvint-corpus-http/main.go:34-40 admits this address; internal/corpusserve/http.go:17-69 performs no authentication or TLS. Expected for a secure remote deployment: a verified external TLS/auth boundary or product-enforced equivalent. Actual: the executable relies on an operator-owned boundary, exactly as DCP-V1-042 and docs/specs/documentation-corpus-v1.md:301-308 declare. This is an intentional experimental limit and a deployment risk, not a confirmed bypass of the accepted contract. Decide whether an authenticated remote profile or a tested reference deployment is appropriate; do not promote external deployment security from local conformance alone.
title: Decide and qualify the security boundary for remote corpus HTTP
